decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “Add ... bookmark”; maker round 2 describes pasting a URL and saving a customized title. Client round 4 confirms: “I pasted the React link.”
decisions.note: The presented URL-based save flow conforms. Prototype/implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1’s feature summary includes “Add” but no metadata collection; maker round 2 subsequently says the flow “now automatically fetches page metadata.” Client round 1 explicitly requests that it “grab the page’s title, description, and icon automatically.”
decisions.note: The client surfaced and requested the missing automatic-metadata behavior. The maker’s “now” revision independently supports that this extended the initial add flow. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 presents an “edit” action. Client round 4 gives broad approval—“edit ... all my saved links”—but neither presentation identifies whether URL, title, description, tags, and note are all editable.
decisions.note: The generic edit claim does not establish either full conformity or a definite divergence from the required field scope. Implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 presents a “delete” action; client round 4 confirms she can “remove” saved links.
decisions.note: The recorded deletion decision conforms. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 explicitly presents “read/unread actions.” Client round 4 confirms she can “flag things to read later.”
decisions.note: Marking bookmarks unread and read is functionally conforming. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 presents “Search.” Client rounds 1 and 4 approve search generally, but no maker presentation establishes that it searches title, description, note, and URL.
decisions.note: The field coverage of search cannot be established; bare general approval does not resolve it. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 presents “tags”; client round 4 confirms she can “tag” saved links.
decisions.note: The recorded tagging capability conforms to assigning tags to bookmarks. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 presents “sorting”; client round 1 reports seeing “sort options,” and round 4 confirms she can sort links.
decisions.note: The presented list-sorting decision conforms. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 presents “grid/list views,” and maker round 2 says the fetched icon appears “on the bookmark card.” The presentations do not establish that every item exposes title, description, tags, and favicon. Client round 1’s “clean and readable” approval does not supply the missing field evidence.
decisions.note: Readability is presented, but complete per-item information exposure cannot be established. Prototype/implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Revised maker presentations enumerate fetched metadata in rounds 2–4 as title, description, website icon, and final redirected URL, omitting the required preview image. Across rounds 2–4 the client repeatedly names only title, description, and icon, then says “That’s exactly the magic I wanted” without identifying the absent preview image.
decisions.note: The revised auto-fill decision remains divergent because REF-BM-02 also requires a preview image. The client’s approval does not qualify as accepted divergence because she never expresses that difference. Implementation review; rounds 2–4 are one clarification-to-disposition sequence.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 presents an edit action; round 2 says “The form stays editable before saving”; round 3 says “all fetched fields remain editable.” Client round 4 confirms the populated information is “still editable” and that saved links can be edited.
decisions.note: Taken together, the recorded before-save editability and continuing edit action conform for auto-collected title and description. Implementation review.
